newsitem.title: CANADA: Placer mine delay not a big worry - analysts.
newsitem.headline: Placer mine delay not a big worry - analysts.

text.p: Mining analysts said news Thursday of a construction delay at Placer Dome Inc's Las Cristinas gold mine in Venezuela was disappointing but not a major cause for alarm unless it drags on for several months.
"For the time being, I'm assuming this is a passing event and I think that is how the market views it," Research Capital Corp analyst Manford Mallory said .
Placer said earlier that construction on the US$576 million Las Cristinas mine did not begin before the end of December as planned. It said the delay was not significant.

Construction was delayed because Placer's joint venture partner -- state-owned Corporacion Venezolana de Guyana, which has a 30 percent stake in the mine -- had not signed the shareholder agreement for the project.

A Placer spokesman said the signing was to have taken place in December and that CVG had given no reason for the delay. Placer was unable to project when CVG would give final approval to the agreement.
"We hope it will be very soon. We are all ready to go. All we need is a signature," the Placer spokesman said. He said CVG had offered no explanation for the delay.
Mining analysts said delays were not uncommon in such projects and they did not think the delay signalled deeper problems with the development.

"Eventually it will happen. It's not a major worry at this point...(but) if after three to six months they still haven't signed, then we start so say, 'This is not so good,'" said one analyst who declined to be named.

Progress on Las Cristinas was slow even before Placer announced a decision to go ahead with the mine last summer. It postponed that decision several times while negotiating with the Venezuelan government on issues including taxes and export restrictions on gold.
Placer said all those issues had been resolved and were not a factor in the construction delay.

Some analysts speculated that CVG's hesitation might reflect financing difficulties, but Placer said this was not the case. The Placer spokesman said CVG will pay for its share of the mine by installing power lines to the site in southeastern Venezuela and financing was not a concern.

Las Cristinas was originally scheduled to begin producing gold in the fourth quarter of 1998. The mine is projected to produce 450,000 ounces of gold a year for at least 16 years and is a big part of Placer's growth strategy.

Placer is planning to build several new mines in the coming years including Pipeline in Nevada. It also cut a deal Thursday with Highlands Gold Ltd of Australia that will raise its stake in the Porgera gold mine in Papua New Guinea to 50 percent.
Meanwhile Placer is also seeking to bid for Bre-X Minerals Ltd and its rich gold discovery in Indonesia.

Placer is lobbying the Indonesian government to consider a proposal it made for a US$5 billion merger with Bre-X, which has been negotiating with Barrick Gold Corp. Analysts said the delay in Venezuela did not appear likely to hurt Placer's effort in Indonesia.
